howTheseWereProduced: Minted for the PRUVZ-88 release by the repository test fixture (test/helpers/mint.mjs): an ephemeral trust registry (one active trust root, one active evidence key), seals over the published examples/valid/verified-refund.packet.json through the canonical commitment, an RFC 6962 log with two signed checkpoints and their consistency proof, and a synthetic RFC 3161 authority (self-signed root CA plus a timestamping leaf whose sole, critical extended key usage is id-kp-timeStamping) whose root PEM is published here for pinning. The private keys were ephemeral and discarded; nothing here is a production identity. Expected reports were produced by lib/verify.mjs at release time; a conformant second-runtime verifier (PRUVZ-97) must reproduce every verdict, reason-code set and dimension status exactly.

cases.description: A complete coherent bundle — packet, seals, inclusion and consistency proofs, trust-registry chain, and witnessed anchors verified against the pinned authority root. The only reachable FULLY_VERIFIED.
The same bundle verified without pinned timestamp-authority roots: bindings are checked, receipts are not authenticated, and the verdict honestly degrades.
No anchors at all, as a PRE_CUSTOMER_DEFAULT deployment produces today: the cost-gated capability is reported absent and the verdict can never be FULLY_VERIFIED.
One item of the packet was altered after sealing. The recomputed commitment digest no longer matches what the seal names: NOT_VERIFIED, never a downgrade to partial.
A seal signature that does not verify under the registry key is a refusal.

The anchoring runtimeDivergence boundary, at bundle level: the altered token still BINDS (its messageImprint is untouched), so a binding-only implementation accepts it — and a verifier performing authority verification MUST refuse it.
Proof material without the packet payload (retention deleted the record; the holder kept the export). Reported honestly as retained proof, never as payload availability.
No trust-registry documents: nothing ties any signature to a recognized identity. Content self-consistency is still checked; origin stays honestly NOT_CHECKED.
A pin naming a different trust root refuses the chain outright: a verifier with the wrong anchor must never quietly accept a substituted registry.
